key_insight: Distributed quantum-centric supercomputing combines fragment-level quantum calculations with generative learning to reconstruct molecular solutions at lower computational cost.
engineering_relevance: Splitting electronic-structure problems into parallel subsystems reduces qubit requirements, circuit depth, sampling budgets, and classical diagonalization demands.
method: Solve molecular fragments with physics-informed generative sample-based quantum diagonalization (PIGen-SQD).
Optimize local-to-global bit assignments to assemble a mapped tensor product state.
Use a second generative module to identify dominant global configurations and recover inter-fragment correlations.
evidence_signal: For water and formamide dimers, the abstract reports up to 95% smaller diagonalization dimensions and an order-of-magnitude improvement in energy accuracy over conventional SQD; a 120-qubit water hexamer was split into six 20-qubit subsystems with excellent agreement with classical references.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on recovering cross-fragment correlations; the hexamer demonstration uses a dimeric approximation whose reliability for more strongly coupled systems remains to be established.
paper_title: Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions
